Title: Environmental Drivers of Microbial Respiration in Forest Soils
Authors: Wang Qiang, Zhao Lei
Year: 2022

1. Introduction
Soil microbial activity is sensitive to environmental shifts. Earlier work suggested contrasting responses.

2. Methods
We conducted a three-year nitrogen addition experiment in temperate broadleaf forests with four treatment levels.

3. Results
Under experimental conditions, nitrogen addition significantly increased microbial respiration by 28.5% compared to the control group (p < 0.01). Furthermore, temperature elevation enhanced enzyme activity across all sampled plots. However, elevated carbon dioxide did not increase fungal biomass in the topsoil layer.

4. Discussion
These results demonstrate that nutrient availability strongly governs soil metabolic output.
